name: go-iec61850
description: IEC 61850 in one library: MMS client and SCL-driven server, GOOSE and Sampled Values publishers and subscribers, and SCL parsing, with logical nodes, reports, controls and control blocks as first-class Go types.
highlights: MMS client: browse, typed reads and writes, datasets, URCB and BRCB reports with EntryID resume, direct, SBO and SBOw controls, setting groups, journals and files.
SCL-driven MMS server with a report engine, the control state machine with CommandTermination, setting groups and journals. One SetValue call drives reports, journals, GOOSE and Sampled Values.

GOOSE (IEC 61850-8-1): publisher with stNum, sqNum and MinTime to MaxTime retransmission, and a supervised subscriber validated against SCL. Server GoCBs are published on data change and readable and writable over MMS.

Sampled Values (IEC 61850-9-2, 9-2LE): drift-free publisher with noASDU batching, and a subscriber that counts loss, duplicates and reordering without allocating per frame. Server MSVCBs are published at their sample rate and exposed over MMS.
Raw Ethernet on Linux (AF_PACKET) and macOS and the BSDs (BPF), plus an in-memory hub with fault injection for tests.
Interop tested in CI against four independent stacks, libiec61850, IEC61850bean, dscsystems/go-iec61850 and iec61850-rust, in both directions, with GOOSE and Sampled Values on a Docker bridge.
Stable v1 API, at least 90% coverage in every package, fuzzed MMS, GOOSE, SV and SCL decoders, and chaos tests. Not certified, and not yet validated against physical IEDs.

name: go-mms
description: MMS (ISO 9506) client and server with the full ISO upper-layer stack, the transport underneath IEC 61850: typed errors, metrics, retries and graceful shutdown, fuzzed and interop tested.
highlights: Client and server for variable access, named variable lists, files, journals, information reports and Status, over COTP and TPKT on TCP port 102, with optional TLS.
Built to run unattended: errors that work with errors.Is and errors.As, a Metrics interface, connection retry with backoff and jitter, association and handshake timeouts, and Server.Shutdown.
A cancelled request no longer tears down its association, and a silent peer can no longer block the listener.
57 fuzz targets, at least 90% coverage in every package, and an end-to-end test of every exported method between its own client and server.
Interop tested in both directions against libiec61850, dscsystems/go-iec61850 and iec61850-rust, with 120 passing scenarios against libiec61850.

name: go-s7comm
description: Siemens S7 client: read and write DBs, inputs, outputs and markers, discovery and SZL diagnostics.

name: go-sunspec
description: SunSpec over Modbus, both sides: discovers and decodes 112 built-in models into typed, scaled values, and serves simulated or real SunSpec devices.

name: go-iec61850-model
description: The IEC 61850 information model without a transport: an edition-aware catalog of logical nodes, data objects, CDCs and data attributes from the official NSD files, with reference validation, type resolution and semantic mapping.
highlights: Imports the official machine-readable namespace definitions (NSD, IEC 61850-7-7) and embeds a catalog of the 12 official namespaces, so lookups need no files.

Edition-aware: several releases of a namespace side by side, explicit profiles, and an ambiguity error instead of a silent merge when two namespaces define the same name (IEC 61850-7-420 and IEC TR 61850-90-9 both define DBAT).
Parses and validates references such as LD0/MMXU1.Hz.mag.f[MX] and resolves them down to their basic type, with functional constraints and presence conditions.
Semantic hints (quantity, phase, unit) from explicit rules for MMXU, MMXN and MMTR, always marked as OT Fabric interpretation and never changing the normative model.
Ontology helpers: a typed concept graph with traversal and JSON export.
No MMS, GOOSE, Sampled Values or SCL runtime. It is the model layer; communication lives in go-iec61850 and go-mms.
Includes nsdctl, the command-line tool for inspecting, validating, comparing and generating from NSD packages.

name: go-sparkplugb
description: Sparkplug B 3.0.0 over MQTT for Go: edge node, primary host application and application roles, with birth and death certificates, primary host awareness, server walking, aliases, sequence checks and the full typed metric codec.
highlights: Three roles in one library: an edge node with devices (package edge), a primary host application that publishes STATE (package host), and an application that tracks nodes without STATE (package app).
Session state as Sparkplug 3.0.0 defines it: NBIRTH and DBIRTH, NDEATH as the MQTT will with bdSeq, DDEATH, rebirth on Node Control/Rebirth, and births that wait for the primary host's STATE.
Server walking: when the primary host goes offline the edge node publishes NDEATH, disconnects and starts a new session on the next broker of ServerURLs.

The host checks seq, holds messages a broker delivers out of order and applies them in sequence, and asks for a rebirth only when a gap stays open; an NDEATH of an earlier session (by bdSeq) is ignored.
Every Sparkplug datatype: all scalars, arrays, DataSets, Templates (definitions and instances) and property sets, with metric aliases and quality codes.

MQTT 3.1.1 over TCP, TLS or WebSocket through Eclipse Paho; any other MQTT client plugs in through the mqtt.Transport interface. context.Context on every blocking call, log/slog logging and metrics callbacks.
Tested on every push against six independent Sparkplug B stacks on four MQTT brokers with sparkplugb-interop. Not run against the official Sparkplug TCK, and not listed as Sparkplug Compatible.
MIT-licensed, except the generated Protobuf code in proto/, which derives from Eclipse Tahu's sparkplug_b.proto and stays under EPL-2.0.

name: go-profinet
description: PROFINET IO-Controller and IO-Device: DCP, LLDP, records, I&M, diagnosis, alarms, cyclic RT data, shared device, MRP rings and GSDML. Raw Ethernet on Linux, macOS and Windows. No dependencies.
highlights: IO-Controller: finds devices by station name with DCP, optionally assigns their address, connects in legacy (RT_CLASS_1) or advanced (RT_CLASS_2) startup, writes parameters, exchanges cyclic data, acknowledges alarms and reconnects after a failure, one lifecycle per device.

IO-Device: DCP responder with Hello, LLDP, the RPC server for Connect, Read, Write, Control and Release, several ARs, shared device, process, diagnosis and plug alarms, I&M0 to I&M4, port data and port checks, with optional persistence of name, address and I&M.
Media redundancy on multiport devices: MRP client, manager and automatic manager on a software switch, plus a read-only SNMP agent with MIB-II and the LLDP-MIB.
GSDML: parse, validate against an independent schema catalog, convert to device models and generate a device's own file; a safe inspector for GSDX containers.

Raw Ethernet on Linux (AF_PACKET), macOS and the BSDs (BPF) and Windows (Npcap), and an in-memory virtual Ethernet with seeded faults, so a controller and devices run in one process without privileges.
Interop tested in CI against p-net, pnio-rs, profinet-py and pnio-dcp, two MRP implementations and Net-SNMP, with Wireshark and scapy decoding every capture: 248 checks pass, none fail.
Not certified by PI and no conformance claim. No IRT, PROFIsafe or PROFINET security classes; cyclic timing runs on Go timers, not a real-time OS.

name: go-canbus
description: The CAN transport for Go: classical CAN, CAN FD and CAN XL frames on Linux SocketCAN, serial-line (slcan) adapters on every OS and a virtual bus, with ISO-TP, capture and replay in seven trace formats, and DBC, KCD and ARXML databases with a signal codec and a Go code generator. go-canopen runs on it. No cgo.
highlights: Frames: classical CAN with 11- and 29-bit identifiers, CAN FD with bit rate switching and error state indicator, remote and error frames, and CAN XL with priority, VCID, SDU type and up to 2048 bytes; filters with the exact semantics of Linux CAN_RAW_FILTER.

Transports: Linux SocketCAN with kernel filters, timestamps, drop accounting and allocation-free I/O; serial-line (slcan) adapters such as CANable, CANtact and USBtin on Linux, macOS and Windows; a deterministic virtual bus with seeded faults; one Bus shared by many filtered subscriptions.
Interface administration through rtnetlink, kept apart from the transport: list and inspect interfaces, bit timing and error counters, bit rates, CAN FD, restart, vcan and vxcan.

ISO-TP (ISO 15765-2) in userspace and through the Linux kernel: normal, extended and mixed addressing, flow control with block size, STmin, WAIT and OVERFLOW, padding, CAN FD and messages above 4095 bytes.
Traces: candump, lossless JSON Lines, pcap and pcapng (checked against tcpdump and Wireshark), Vector ASC and BLF, PEAK TRC, with streaming replay at original, scaled or maximum speed.

Databases: DBC and KCD read and write, AUTOSAR 4 ARXML read, with Intel and Motorola byte order, signed, float, scaling, value tables, simple and extended multiplexing and exact 64-bit raw values; typed Go generated from a database.

Interop tested in CI on Linux virtual CAN against can-utils and the kernel's ISO-TP, python-can, socketcan-rs, Scapy, python-can-isotp, cantools and canmatrix: 170 scenarios pass, none fail. Kernels 6.1 to 7.0 in micro-VMs.

No ISO or CiA conformance claim, and not yet tested on real CAN hardware: virtual CAN shows frame encoding and protocol logic, not bit timing, arbitration or bus-off. No vendor adapters (PEAK, Kvaser, Vector) yet. CANopen runs on top in go-canopen; J1939 and UDS are not implemented.

name: go-canopen
description: CANopen (CiA 301) and CANopen FD on go-canbus: object dictionary, SDO and USDO, NMT, heartbeat, PDOs and MPDOs, SYNC, EMCY, TIME, LSS, a complete device and a CiA 302 network manager, EDS/DCF files, typed Go from an EDS and the CiA 402 drive profile. No cgo.
highlights: The CiA 301 services: an object dictionary with access rights, limits, node-ID relative defaults, hooks and watchers; SDO client and server with expedited, segmented and block transfer; NMT master and slave with both resets; heartbeat, node guarding and life guarding; SYNC with the synchronous window, EMCY and TIME.

PDOs with every transmission type, inhibit time, event timer, RTR and deadline monitoring, the CiA 301 reconfiguration rules and remote configuration; multiplexed PDOs (DAM and SAM) with scanner and dispatcher lists.

A complete device built from a dictionary, gated by its NMT state, and a network manager: scan, boot procedure, DCF configuration, the CiA 302 network boot-up with an optional LSS step, concise DCF configuration, program download and one ordered event stream.
LSS (CiA 305) master and slave with Fastscan and automatic node-ID assignment; store and restore of parameters behind 0x1010 and 0x1011.
CANopen FD (CiA 1301) from public sources: the USDO, 64-byte PDOs and 20-byte emergencies. No open reference stack implements it, so it is tested against go-canopen itself only.

EDS and DCF (CiA 306) parsing, validation and writing, typed Go generated from an EDS, the CiA 402 drive profile with a simulated drive and a controller, and a frame dissector checked against Wireshark.
Runs on go-canbus, so the same code works on Linux SocketCAN, slcan adapters on every OS and an in-process virtual bus.

Interop tested against CANopenNode, Lely CANopen and python canopen in both directions on Linux virtual CAN: 1,276 scenarios pass and none fail, with 57 documented differences and 287 skips where a stack lacks a feature. No CiA conformance claim, nothing tested on real CAN hardware yet.

name: go-knx
description: KNX over KNXnet/IP: frames, cEMI and 209 datapoint subtypes, discovery, tunnelling over UDP and TCP, routing, group communication, device management, busmonitor and a KNXnet/IP server with virtual devices, with KNX IP Secure, KNX Data Secure and ETS keyrings. Pure Go, no dependencies, no cgo.
highlights: Frames: KNXnet/IP header, HPAI, every standard DIB, CRI and CRD, core, device management, tunnelling, routing and secure bodies; cEMI L_Data, L_Busmon, L_Raw and property services; TPCI and APCI. Strict codecs that never panic, fuzzed.
Datapoint types 1 to 14, 16 to 22, 26, 29, 232, 242 and 251: 209 subtypes with ranges, units and text formatting and parsing.

Discovery with multicast, directed and extended search and description; a tunnelling client over UDP with sequence handling, retransmission, L_Data.con, heartbeats, NAT and reconnection, and over TCP with tunnelling v2 address requests and feature services.

Routing with ROUTING_BUSY flow control, rate limit and echo suppression; group write, read, respond and subscriptions over a tunnel or routing; device management of interface object properties; busmonitor with TP1 frame decoding.

A KNXnet/IP server for several tunnelling clients over UDP and TCP, with discovery, busmonitor, device management, routing and virtual devices whose group objects store writes and answer reads by their flags. ETS-style tools, Home Assistant through xknx, Calimero and knxd connect to it like to an IP interface.

KNX IP Secure sessions over TCP and UDP and secure routing with timer synchronisation, in client and server; KNX Data Secure for group communication with S-A_Sync and the surrogate role; ETS keyrings read and written. Implemented from public sources and verified against xknx and Calimero.

Interop tested in both directions against Calimero 3.0-M1, knxd 0.14.73, xknx 4.0.0 and KNXUltimate 6.3.1, with a raw probe for malformed input: the full knx-interop matrix passes 423 results, none fail.

Not KNX certified and no conformance claim; not yet tested with a physical KNX IP interface. No TP1, RF or powerline media directly, no ETS project import, no point-to-point Data Secure beyond the surrogate service.

name: go-otfp
description: Find out which OT protocol an endpoint speaks, and read the device's identity, with safe connection-level probes. 18 protocols, graded confidence, zero runtime dependencies.
highlights: Detects 18 protocols: Modbus TCP, SunSpec, IEC 61850 MMS, Siemens S7comm and S7comm-plus, OPC UA, EtherNet/IP, BACnet/IP, PROFINET IO, DNP3, IEC 60870-5-104, OCPP, IEEE 2030.5, OpenADR 3 and 2.0b, KNXnet/IP, MQTT 3.1.1 and 5, Sparkplug B, CAN over TCP gateways and CANopen through CiA 309-3 gateways.
Safe by design: each protocol gets its standard handshake or one harmless request. It never writes a value, issues a control or changes a device's configuration.

Identify mode sends each protocol's own read-only identity service (Read Device Identification, the CIP Identity object, SZL, MMS Identify, the BACnet Device object, OPC UA GetEndpoints, PROFINET I&M0, the KNXnet/IP description, the CANopen identity object over SDO) and returns vendor, model, version and serial. Sparkplug B is read-only: it subscribes for a bounded window and never publishes.
Port-agnostic over TCP, UDP and TLS: the target port's likely protocols go first, then the rest, so a protocol on a non-standard port is still found.
Graded confidence on one shared scale, with the evidence behind every match and a stable fingerprint signature per result.
An OT-safe mode for production networks: passive probes only, the likely protocols of a port first, and 250 ms between probes.

Validated against 18 reference servers and setups from the OT Fabric interop suites, from pymodbus and open62541 to calimero-server, Mosquitto, HiveMQ CE and CANopenNode. End-to-end fuzzed, tested against hostile and chaos peers and a cross-protocol false-positive matrix, with at least 90% test coverage in every package.
Standard library only, so it drops into any Go program; Go 1.26 or later. Ships with the otprobe command-line tool.

name: otprobe
description: The command-line tool included with go-otfp: point it at an endpoint or a host and it tells you which OT protocol answers, with what confidence, and which device is behind it.
highlights: otprobe detect 10.0.0.5:502 --identify probes one endpoint and reads the device identity; a bare host sweeps the well-known OT ports.
tcp://, udp:// and tls:// targets, so BACnet/IP, PROFINET, EtherNet/IP and KNXnet/IP over UDP and Modbus/TCP Security or wss:// over TLS are covered.
--safe keeps to passive probes and paces them 250 ms apart, to stay under OT intrusion detection thresholds.
Text output for people, --format table for one row per probe and --format json with a versioned schema for scripts.
Stable exit codes for automation: 0 detected, 1 no match, 2 usage, 3 invalid input, 4 unreachable, 5 timeout, 7 matched below high confidence, 10 interrupted or internal error.
--trace shows the raw probe and response bytes; shell completion for bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell.
--canopen-node picks the CANopen node whose identity is read through a CiA 309-3 gateway in --identify mode.
One-line install on Linux, macOS and Windows from get.otfabric.io. otprobe is a nested module, so building from source is make build in a go-otfp checkout rather than go install.

name: LAN Tracker
description: A history of what is connected to your OT networks: which MAC held which IP and when, names, DHCP leases, TCP reachability and duplicate addresses. Passive by default.
highlights: Answers questions after the fact: who held 192.168.110.51 yesterday at 10:15, since when two devices claim the same IP, and when port 502 on an inverter stopped answering.
Passive by default: listens to ARP, DHCP, mDNS, DNS answers, LLDP and the kernel neighbour table, and sends nothing until you enable active discovery for an interface.

Optional active discovery inside a strict safety envelope: ARP sweeps, ping and plain TCP connects with no payload, 5 probe starts per second in all by default, excluded addresses and a persistent kill switch. Preview any scan with scan plan.
DHCPv4 in depth: the servers and relays that answer, checked against an allowlist, each client's exchanges, and a lease history with the gateway and DNS servers handed out.
Events for every material change (new devices, IP changes, duplicate IPs, rogue DHCP servers, TCP state changes, collection gaps), in its database and in the systemd journal.
Does not identify equipment: no models, firmware or banner grabbing. Your own description on a device is the only statement about what it is.
One static binary under systemd on Linux edge devices (Raspberry Pi CM4, RevPi Connect, x86 edge boxes), with a local CLI, a REST API on a Unix socket and Prometheus metrics. No data leaves the box.

name: sparkplugb-interop

name: sunspec-interop
description: SunSpec reference stacks in containers behind one contract: the SunSpec Alliance's pysunspec2 and cB-Sigma's sunspec and sunspec-sim, as devices and clients, with fixtures from the common models to the IEEE 1547 DER curves.

name: SunSpec Explorer
description: Connect to a SunSpec inverter, meter or battery and see every model it exposes fully decoded. Read once or poll, record and export, without ever writing to the device.
highlights: Every point of every model decoded: value with units, scale factor, enum and bitfield names, raw value and register address. Not-implemented points are labeled as such, never shown as 65535.
Repeating and nested groups shown as instances, and raw registers for models without a known schema.
Poll at whole-second intervals with stale values marked, and record samples as JSON Lines or CSV.
Export a JSON snapshot, the points as CSV, or a device file that sunspecctl serve turns back into the same device.
Modbus/TCP, RTU over TCP, Modbus/TCP Security (TLS) and serial RS-485. Read-only: only function codes 3 and 4 reach the wire.
A desktop application for macOS, Windows and Linux, or a daemon on a gateway with the same interface in any browser over an SSH tunnel.

name: Modbus Trace Explorer
description: Open a packet trace of Modbus/TCP traffic and see it in Modbus terms: every request with its response, per device, per poll and per register. Then export the real traffic to replay as a simulated device.
highlights: Latency per device and per unit behind a gateway, with quantiles and a histogram: which device holds up the cycle.
Poll plans per client: what each client reads, how often, how regularly and how often the answer changes. Duplicate polling and cycles that overrun their interval show at once.
Exceptions, unanswered requests and gateway errors explained in words, with a filter grammar such as status:exception unit:4 addr:holding/4096-4160.
What was read and written per device, and the values of one register over time with the writes marked. Every connection with its role, resets, gaps and retransmissions.

Export one device, the current filter or everything as an MBCAP capture, with a preview of what goes in and why the rest stays out, ready for modbusctl server replay. Also CSV, JSON Lines and a pcapng sub-trace.
Reads pcap and pcapng from tcpdump, Wireshark, dumpcap or tshark, ring buffers and gzip files as they are, and MBCAP captures. A million rows page, filter and sort in milliseconds.
Read-only and offline: it never talks to devices, never writes to Modbus and does not capture live. A desktop application for macOS, Windows and Linux.
